material.title: Speaking Test 1 - Three Parts
material.description: Sample speaking test with Parts 1, 2, and 3

parts.description: Introduction and interview. The examiner asks questions about familiar topics such as home, family, work, studies, and interests.
prompts: Good morning/afternoon. My name is [name]. What's your name?
Can you tell me a bit about yourself?
Do you work or are you a student?
What do you like to do in your free time?
follow_up_prompts: How often do you do that?
How long have you been doing this?
Do many people do this in your country?
Is that a hobby or something you do professionally?

parts.description: Individual long turn. The candidate is given a task card with a topic and several points to cover. The candidate has 1 minute to prepare and then speaks for 1-2 minutes. The examiner does not ask questions during this part.
prompts:
Describe a memorable journey you have taken.
You should say:
- Where you went
- Who you traveled with
- What you did there
- And explain why it was memorable

Describe a book or film that you enjoyed.
You should say:
- What it was about
- When you read/watched it
- Why you liked it
- And explain what you learned from it
follow_up_prompts: Would you go back to that place?
Do many people visit that place?
What was the most interesting part?
Would you recommend this to others?

parts.description: Discussion. The examiner asks follow-up questions related to the Part 2 topic and related abstract themes. This part involves a more in-depth discussion.
prompts: Do you think travel is important? Why?
How has travel changed in recent years?
What are the benefits and drawbacks of travel?
How do different types of media influence people's choices?
How important are books and films in modern society?
How has technology changed the way we consume entertainment?
follow_up_prompts: Do you agree with that viewpoint?
How might this change in the future?
What is your opinion on this trend?

band_descriptors.9: Speaks fluently with only rare repetition or self-correction; any hesitation is content-related rather than language-related; develops topics coherently and appropriately
band_descriptors.8: Speaks fluently with only occasional repetition or self-correction; hesitation is usually content-related; develops and links ideas well but occasionally lacks focus
band_descriptors.7: Speaks at length without noticeable effort or loss of coherence; may demonstrate language-related hesitation; links ideas but may not always do so fluently
band_descriptors.6: Produces longer turns without noticeable effort but may repeat themselves; uses basic connectors but some ideas lack clarity or focus
band_descriptors.5: Usually maintains flow of speech but uses repetition, self-correction and/or slow speech to keep going; limited use of connectors

band_descriptors.9: Uses a wide vocabulary range fluently and appropriately; skillfully uses uncommon words and expressions; topic-specific vocabulary is accurate
band_descriptors.8: Uses a range of vocabulary with some precision; uses paraphrase successfully; some use of topic-specific vocabulary
band_descriptors.7: Uses a range of vocabulary; topic-specific vocabulary is used accurately; occasional inaccuracy in word choice
band_descriptors.6: Uses adequate vocabulary for the topics discussed; attempts topic-specific vocabulary but may be imprecise
band_descriptors.5: Uses vocabulary that is mostly appropriate, though sometimes inaccurate; limited range; repetition of the same words

band_descriptors.9: Uses a full range of structures naturally and appropriately; produces error-free speech regularly
band_descriptors.8: Uses a range of complex structures; generally produces error-free speech; occasional errors or inappropriacies
band_descriptors.7: Uses a range of simple and complex structures; makes only occasional grammatical errors; errors do not reduce communication
band_descriptors.6: Uses a mix of simple and complex structures; errors are common but do not usually impede communication
band_descriptors.5: Limited range of structures; makes frequent errors which may impede communication; some important mistakes

band_descriptors.9: Exhibits clear, natural pronunciation; stress and intonation are well-managed; may show slight traces of an accent
band_descriptors.8: Pronunciation is mostly clear; L1 accent is evident but does not noticeably affect intelligibility; stress and intonation are mostly accurate
band_descriptors.7: Pronunciation is clearly intelligible; L1 accent is noticeable; intonation is reasonable; some words mispronounced
band_descriptors.6: Pronunciation is generally intelligible; L1 accent is quite noticeable; some errors in stress and intonation
band_descriptors.5: Pronunciation is generally intelligible; some errors in pronunciation may occasionally cause misunderstanding; wide range of errors in stress, rhythm, and intonation

source.notes: Example speaking test structure and prompts modeled on official IELTS format.
